chains.title: TCF7L2 binding may be reduced on the C allele

links.claim: TCF7L2 is a leading candidate because it is expressed and has a ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT116. QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger binding to T than C, but its gated model is mapped from TCF7, not TCF7L2-specific, and the modeled site is weak; thus the allele-specific prediction is indirect and the ChIP peak may reflect another site in the element.
The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the reported chromatin-mark maxima do not establish activity of this element in HCT116.

POU5F1B is a candidate, not a demonstrated target: it is nearby and has the top L2G score in two low-PIP credible sets for non-CRC traits, but no significant GTEx eQTL or functional enhancer-to-gene link is reported. Open Targets supports gene-level CRC relevance, not this variant-to-gene link.
HCT116 is a plausible context because TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant and expression are reported there; allele-specific occupancy has not been measured.
POU5F1B has CRC-related gene-level support, including literature on its effects in colon cancer cells, but the evidence does not show that this variant changes POU5F1B or CRC risk.

predictions: If TCF7L2 binds the variant-overlapping site in HCT116, T should show greater TCF7L2-specific binding or occupancy than C.
A variant-dependent POU5F1B expression effect, if present, should depend on TCF7L2; binding direction alone does not predict expression direction.
falsified_if: A TCF7L2-specific assay finds no reproducible T-versus-C binding difference under conditions where TCF7L2 binds the sequence.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401265:T>C, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 40 occupied (6 with a strong site), 5 of 103 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 11 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 517 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 5 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.

TCF7L2 (HMG/Sox, 3 models; QBiC-SELEX coverage: mapped models only): best model TCF7_eDBD_TCGGAC40NCCA_KS_yin2017_0_3_7mer (a CIS-BP-mapped model of TCF7), z -8.8, effect -0.429: ref allele binds more (|z| above the gate), but between weak k-mers. 63.61 TPM, rank 53 of 1626 TFs in DepMap:ACH-000971 (HCT 116).
